title: Morgan Stanley Promotes Fewest to Most Elite Rank Since 2002
description: Jan.15 -- Morgan Stanley carried out its smallest wave of annual promotions to the firm's top rank of managing director since 2002. Bloomberg's Sonali Basak reports on "Bloomberg Daybreak: Americas."

asr.full_text: Let's come to a second story. And that's Morgan Stanley promoting Few People. What did you make of this? So there's two things of this. One, it's interesting that Morgan Stanley and Goldman are keeping their ranks as elite as humanly possible. That's kind of the goal, to get there one day. Something I think about a lot is as they do this, how do they retain talent? Because if you're making it harder for people to get to the very, very top, you already have a situation where a lot of the younger people also have been turning over at a high rate, right? People are moving into private equity and hedge funds and technology, and so how then do they rise up the bank to the very high levels? On the flip side, if you go back to times where like, everyone was just promoted at the same time and then there was no exclusivity, so then there was also no challenge and at some point, you just kind tapped out. There's also that argument on the flip side. — That's the gold standard, to be a partner at one of these firms and so... — There's a million of them and all of your buddies have it, so what's the point? — Exactly. Something that's interesting too is the numbers behind this also and how many strikes are making in diversity. Within the US only seventeen percent of the class in Morgan Stanley are Asian, only 4 percent are black, and 4 percent are Hispanic. There's a higher number of women being promoted this year. But it's still only about 25 percent of the promotions at this time. Obviously, Morgan Stanley and every bank on Wall Street would like to get better numbers there. MADELINE GONZALEZ- HMM-HMM. Yeah. Absolutely, especially when it comes to the overall competition.
